data.title: Ukraine-Russia truce spotlights rare thaw between officials
data.description: KYIV - Russia’s human rights ombudsman Yana Lantratova nodded along as her counterpart from Kyiv, Dmytro Lubinets, spoke Ukrainian to brief the media about the longest truce between their warring countries.

data.title: Baghdad's first Jewish museum opens its doors
data.description: BAGHDAD - Dozens of visitors have begun flocking to a new museum opened by Iraq's Jewish community, the first of its kind, amid ongoing efforts by the minority to preserve its heritage.

data.title: Spain working ‘tirelessly’ to restore trust in trains
data.description: MADRID - Spain will work “tirelessly” to restore confidence in its high-speed trains, the transport minister said Tuesday, after a collision last week killed 69 people in the country’s second such disaster this year.

data.title: Students blockade dozens of French schools and universities
data.description: PARIS - Students blockaded dozens of high schools and universities across France on Tuesday to maintain pressure on the government over education reforms as trade unions prepared for a nationwide strike.

data.title: Italy holds security talks after freezer cyberattacks
data.description: ROME - Italy’s government held emergency talks with intelligence chiefs on Tuesday following cyberattacks on supermarket freezer systems in at least 11 European countries.

data.title: King Charles to voice ‘sorrow’ for slavery
data.description: ST JOHN’S, Antigua and Barbuda - King Charles III will express “sincere sorrow” about Britain’s role in slavery when he opens a meeting of Commonwealth leaders on Tuesday, as Prime Minister Andy Burnham begins talks over a formal apology.

data.title: Israeli opposition considers how to oust Netanyahu
data.description: HERZLIYA, Israel - The Israeli opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot gathered on Tuesday for the first time since elections as they strategise how to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, with divisions on whether to ally with Arab lawmakers.

data.title: Americans vote in polls that could shake Trump presidency
data.description: WASHINGTON - Americans began voting on Tuesday in pivotal midterm elections with Democrats hoping to seize control of Congress and impose the first significant checks on Donald Trump’s chaotic second term in the White House.

data.title: Iran hangs two young men for protest-linked offences
data.description: Iran on Tuesday hanged two young men on charges related to nationwide protests in January, as rights groups accused authorities of subjecting them to torture and an unfair trial.

data.title: Bangladesh garment workers clash with police
data.description: DHAKA - Paramilitary forces were deployed in industrial suburbs around the Bangladesh capital as protests by garment sector workers demanding a wage hike stretched into their fourth day on Tuesday, defying calls to return to factories.

data.title: China Eastern Airlines ex-chairman sentenced to 14 years for bribery
data.description: BEIJING — Liu Shaoyong, ​former chairman of ​China ‌Eastern Airlines, was sentenced to 14 years in prison over bribery, ​China Central Television ( CCTV ) reported on Tuesday.

data.title: Hong Kong to sentence activist Joshua Wong on Thursday
data.description: HONG KONG — A Hong Kong court will sentence pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong on Thursday, according to the judiciary's website, in a second national security trial that could see him jailed for life.

data.title: US signals progress in Iran talks to avert flare-up
data.description: WASHINGTON — United States President Donald Trump signaled progress on Monday in talks with Iran to avoid a return to war, as Tehran reported "intensive" exchanges while offering to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under strict conditions.

data.title: Sea drone makers compete in Taiwan for soaring investment
data.description: TAINAN — Silver-hulled sea drones skim across the water as part of an exhibition in Taiwan where local and foreign companies are competing for a share of surging government investment in uncrewed vehicles to deter China.

data.title: 'Cursed' Peru town hopes Pope Leo brings better luck
data.description: CHICLAYO — A luckless Peruvian town that has for centuries been dismissed as cursed is hoping for a new lease on life when Pope Leo visits this month.

data.title: Mexican investigators raid storage unit rented by Thomas Markle
data.description: TIJUANA — Mexican authorities raided a storage unit rented by Meghan Markle's estranged father as part of an ongoing investigation into alleged child sex abuse material, the state prosecutor's office told Agence France-Presse ( AFP ) on Monday.

data.title: Pyongyang blasts FBI allegations as it test-fires missiles
data.description: SEOUL - Pyongyang blasted on Monday the FBI's allegations it was behind the theft of US$6 billion from cryptocurrency platform Binance, as it test-fired strategic cruise missiles in a new display of its weapons capabilities.

data.title: US strategy links Myanmar peace talks to rare-earth access
data.description: WASHINGTON - Washington aims to use peace diplomacy in Myanmar as a way to expand US influence and potentially gain access to the country's rare-earth deposits, according to a recently published State Department strategy document.

data.title: Americans vote in midterms set to upend Trump presidency
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Americans deliver their verdict on Donald Trump's tumultuous second presidency Tuesday in midterm elections that threaten to shatter his grip on Washington, with Democrats poised to seize the House and challenge for control of the Senate.

data.title: Multinational Ukraine force to hold first exercise in Poland
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Some 2,800 troops from 10 European countries will this month stage in Poland the first exercise of a new multinational force in support of Ukraine, London and Paris said on Tuesday.

data.title: Trial of accused USS Cole attack mastermind opens at Guantanamo
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Jury selection began on Monday in the long-delayed trial of Abd al-Rahim al-Nashiri, the accused mastermind of the 2000 attack on the USS Cole warship that left 17 American sailors dead.

data.title: Top Arab-Israeli leader tells AFP opposition must join to oust Netanyahu
data.description: NAZARETH (ISRAEL) - The leader of the largest Arab-majority party in the incoming Israeli parliament told AFP on Monday that it was time for reluctant opposition members to accept "political reality" and join forces to unseat Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

data.title: Caught cold: fridge cyberattack highlights internet gadget weaknesses
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Cyberattacks affecting supermarket refrigeration systems in several European countries on Monday highlighted the risks associated with connecting industrial equipment to the internet.

data.title: Prayers, anticipation await Pope Leo in Argentine care home
data.description: CLAYPOLE (ARGENTINA) - A home for disabled people on the outskirts of Buenos Aires was full of anticipation as it prepared to receive Pope Leo XIV, amid a growing controversy over state assistance for those with special needs in Argentina.

data.title: Ukraine, Russia see emergency alert systems hacked
data.description: KYIV (UKRAINE) - Emergency alert systems in Russia and Ukraine were hit in cyber attacks overnight leading into Monday, with fake warnings of possible nuclear strikes broadcast to users in both countries.

data.title: Belgian PM offers to quit over budget impasse
data.description: BRUSSELS (BELGIUM) - Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever tendered his resignation to King Philippe on Monday over deadlocked budget talks, but the monarch deferred his decision until after a new meeting Friday.

data.title: Russia resumes strikes on Kherson after truce ends
data.description: KYIV (UKRAINE) - Russia resumed strikes on the southern Ukrainian city of Kherson on Monday after the end of a local ceasefire in the area -- the longest truce in the war raging between the neighbours since 2022 -- Kyiv said.

data.title: Israel army withdraws after Hebron operation
data.description: HEBRON (PALESTINIAN TERRITORIES) - Israeli troops withdrew on Monday from an area of the occupied West Bank's largest city that they had evacuated of its Palestinian residents, following an attack that killed two soldiers in October.

data.title: Bangladesh garment workers clash with police protesting higher wages
data.description: ASHULIA — Thousands of Bangladeshi garment workers blocked a major highway and clashed with police on Monday, demanding a monthly minimum wage more than double their current pay, as protests spread across industrial hubs.

data.title: Limited French school protests resume as holidays end
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - French students returning from autumn holidays blocked some high schools on Monday, determined to reinvigorate a protest movement despite government concessions during the break.
